newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN TRADE SURPLUS WON'T CONTINUE BIG RISES--MOF.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN TRADE SURPLUS WON'T CONTINUE BIG RISES--MOF.

text.p: Japan's surplus in goods and services trade is not expected to continue large rises, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official told reporters on Friday.
He said a rise in Japan's sales tax on April 1 had been a special factor behind dramatic rises in the surplus in the April-June quarter.

The surplus in goods and services had declined in the past several years due to various factors such as a shift of production facilities to overseas by manufacturers, an increase in imports and deregulation.
These structural shifts in the economy were not expected to change although the surplus in goods and services experienced short-term fluctuations.
He add that the ministry would continue to watch future movements in the surplus.

The Finance Ministry announced earlier on Friday that the surplus in Japan's current account, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, rose 55.8 percent in June from a year earlier to 1.02 trillion yen,
The surplus in merchandise trade alone rose 18.7 percent to 1.1 trillion yen in June from the same month a year earlier.
The surplus in the current account in the January-June period rose 40.4 percent from a year earlier to 5.05 trillion yen, the ministry said.
The surplus in merchandise trade alone in January-June rose 19.6 percent from the same period a year earlier to 5.18 trillion yen.
